problems.problem: Calls and web form inquiries arriving after 4:30 PM on weekdays or over weekends may wait until the next business day for a response, risking lead loss to competitors.
problems.label: hypothesis
problems.basis: The website lists business hours of Monday–Friday, 8am–4:30pm and has no visible automated scheduling or instant response tool on the pages read.

problems.problem: Leads from web forms, phone calls, and paid ads may require manual entry into whatever scheduling or estimating system the team uses, creating potential follow-up delays on free written estimates.
problems.label: hypothesis
problems.basis: The site uses a generic web form and phone number for intake with no visible integration to a field-service management system.

problems.problem: Tracking booked revenue, close rates on written estimates, and cost per booked job across both the Boise, ID and Lexington, KY operations may require manual compilation.
problems.label: hypothesis
problems.basis: The company runs multi-state operations (ID and KY) and loads an ad tracking tag (AW-805112476) on interior pages, but internal reporting practices are not visible publicly.

existingSolutions.solution: Field-service management software (such as ServiceTitan, Housecall Pro, or Jobber) with built-in online booking, automated lead text-back, and estimate follow-up
existingSolutions.addresses: Lead capture, instant response to missed calls/web forms, and automated follow-up on written estimates

existingSolutions.solution: Native CRM and reporting dashboards within off-the-shelf field-service and accounting software
existingSolutions.addresses: Weekly performance tracking across lead sources, estimates, and booked jobs

forgexSolutions.name: Revenue Leak Check
forgexSolutions.description: One-week audit ($500 fixed price, credited toward any fix ordered within 30 days) to measure how many calls, web form leads, and written estimates slip through, especially outside the 8:00 AM–4:30 PM Monday–Friday window.
forgexSolutions.problem: Potential loss of after-hours or unreturned calls, web form inquiries, and open written estimates.
forgexSolutions.whyNotExistingSoftware: Before buying new software or building automations, a baseline audit establishes whether a material leak exists and whether existing tools can be configured to solve it.

forgexSolutions.name: Lead-to-job pipeline
forgexSolutions.description: Automated lead routing ($1,800 setup plus $149/month) that captures every web form submission and lead source within two minutes, sends an immediate reply, and tracks callback completion.
forgexSolutions.problem: Potential delay in responding to web form inquiries and after-hours leads.
forgexSolutions.whyNotExistingSoftware: Website forms often send static notification emails that do not automatically create records in back-office field-service software or trigger immediate SMS/email acknowledgments without custom middleware.

forgexSolutions.name: Owner's Monday numbers
forgexSolutions.description: Weekly one-page summary ($1,200 setup plus $99/month) combining field-service software, accounting, and ad account data into booked revenue, close rate, average ticket, and cost per booked job.
forgexSolutions.problem: Difficulty getting a unified weekly view of ad spend efficiency and estimate close rates across Boise and Lexington operations.
forgexSolutions.whyNotExistingSoftware: Standard field-service dashboards rarely reconcile paid search spend, accounting receivables, and multi-location close rates in a single automated owner digest.

feasibility.explanation: Capturing Squarespace contact form submissions and routing them to SMS/email and a back-office system is technically straightforward, but overall feasibility depends on what field-service, phone, and accounting software Crofts Electric currently uses internally (which is not disclosed on the website).

aiDelivery.explanation: Deterministic workflow automation handles lead ingestion, instant replies, follow-up reminders, and weekly metric aggregation best; AI agents could assist in classifying free-text project descriptions (e.g., panel upgrade vs. commercial fit-out vs. Realtor inspection) or drafting initial responses, with human handoff for electrical scoping and pricing.

humanReview: All electrical technical assessments, code compliance judgments, and written cost estimates must be reviewed and approved by a licensed journeyman or master electrician.

Eligibility verification for advertised discounts (15% new customer initial labor discount, 10% repeat customer discount, and 10% senior/first responder/active military discount) requires staff confirmation.
Any automated customer-facing reply templates must be approved by owner [redacted] before deployment.

risks.description: Automated text or email replies to incoming leads must comply with TCPA opt-in requirements and CAN-SPAM regulations.
An automated assistant must never give electrical safety advice, troubleshooting instructions, or binding price quotes, as improper electrical guidance carries severe safety and liability risks.
Customer contact details, property addresses, and access instructions for Realtor or property management jobs must be transmitted and stored securely with least-privilege access.

commercial.implementationCost: Revenue Leak Check: $500 fixed price (credited in full toward any fix ordered within 30 days); Lead-to-job pipeline: $1,800 setup plus $149/month; Owner's Monday numbers: $1,200 setup plus $99/month.
assumptions: The website advertises percentage discounts (10% and 15%) and free written estimates but publishes no dollar prices or hourly rates, so illustrative commercial value cannot be calculated from site data.

discovery.outreachSubject: Question about lead follow-up and written estimates at Crofts Electric
discovery.outreachBody:
Hi [redacted],

I was reviewing Crofts Electric's Boise website and noticed your team handles a wide mix of residential service upgrades, EV chargers, Realtor code-compliance work, and commercial projects with office hours from 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM Monday through Friday.

At ForgeX, we work with owner-led electrical and home-service contractors to audit and automate lead capture and estimate follow-up—Starting with a fixed-price $500 Revenue Leak Check that looks at how many after-hours calls, web form inquiries, and written estimates slip through the cracks (with the $500 credited in full if you order a fix within 30 days). We do not promise specific revenue outcomes, and if your current software already handles lead intake and reporting well, we will tell you upfront.

Would you be open to a brief call to see if a leak check makes sense for your Boise and Lexington operations?

Best regards,

[FOUNDER_NAME]
[FOUNDER_TITLE], ForgeX
[FOUNDER_PHONE]
[FORGEX_POSTAL_ADDRESS]

If you prefer not to receive future emails from us, simply reply with "unsubscribe" or follow [OPT_OUT_INSTRUCTION].

sourcesUsed.usedFor: Business identity, Boise service area, services offered, operating hours, phone number, Idaho and Kentucky license numbers, discount offers, and front-end script evidence.
Founder identity ([redacted]), parent entity (RC Electric LLC), company history in Lexington, KY and expansion to Boise, ID, and ad tracking tag evidence.
Team composition (journeyman and master electricians only) and licensing qualification descriptions.
Lead intake workflow (contact form and phone call instructions) and promoted 10% discount project categories.
Details on promotional discounts (15% new customer labor discount, 10% repeat customer discount) and commercial/construction bidding approach.
Property management electrical service offerings and consultation workflow.

limitations: The website does not state the exact number of employees in Boise or Lexington, so whether the company falls within ForgeX's 10-to-75 staff range cannot be verified from the site alone.
No dollar prices or hourly service rates appear on the website, preventing an illustrative calculation of commercial value.
Back-office software (such as field-service management, CRM, or accounting systems) is not visible on the public website.
No business email address is published on the pages read; contact is limited to the phone number ([redacted]) and the contact page web form.
One internal link from the About page (https://www.croftselectricboise.com/trusted-experts-boise-electricians-lexington-electricians) returned HTTP 404.

qualification.rationale: Crofts Electric is an owner-led electrical contractor (founded by Master Electrician [redacted]) operating in Boise, ID and Lexington, KY, with evidence of paid lead generation (an advertising tag on its pages) and a public business phone number ([redacted]). However, its headcount (10 to 75 staff) cannot be confirmed from the website, and potential operational problems—such as missed leads outside its 8:00 AM–4:30 PM weekday hours or manual follow-up on free written estimates—remain plausible hypotheses rather than confirmed problems. Under ForgeX's qualification rules, a plausible fit whose problems are hypotheses only qualifies as 'pursue later'.
